authors: Alfons van Marrewijk, Stewart R. Clegg, Tyrone S. Pitsis, Marcel Veenswijk
method: comparative ethnographic case study (Environ, NL; NSTP, Sydney 2000)
definition: No project-governance definition. PPP = 'structural cooperation between public and private parties to deliver some agreed outcome' (p. 591).
stakeholders: Public + private partners; politicians. Environ: EUR800m overrun -> parliamentary inquiry -> politicians demand control -> ministry centralization. NSTP: no-blame alliance culture resolves conflict.
decision_making: Yes (Brief) - comparative case analysis; alliance vs concession decision structures.
temporality_detail: Decade-long PPP phases; political interference framed as disruption to design/culture. No cyclical/electoral clock.
megaproject_detail: Two PPP megaprojects (Environ NL; North Side Tunnel Project, Sydney 2000 Olympics).
misalignment_detail: Political takeover after overrun is a political-time analogue at cabinet scale, but explained via project design/culture, not temporal mismatch.
gaps: Rejects Flyvbjerg 'deception' thesis; explains outcomes via design/culture. Establishes design x culture lens the RQ can layer an electoral clock onto; no recurring political clock.
key_quotes: 'structural cooperation between public and private parties to deliver some agreed outcome' (p. 591).
Project design and project cultures 'play a role in determining how managers and partners cooperate' (abstract).
coding_notes: Emic/ethnographic; origin of the widely-cited PPP definition. Clegg co-authors both this and Dille et al. (2018) - cross-reference.
